title: Four coarse stroke features recur across scripts while the ordered p84 form remains unverified at its source
statement: Ardıç's highlighted p84 crop and its repeated entry 42 do not identify a folio or line. A documented search of the 204 numbered Yale canvases found approximate analogues and no verified source. A known f8r control was recovered at rank 1 near its correct scale and rank 19 across scales. The strongest enlarged candidate verified on the native scan, f76v, has a closed triangular projection at the left junction and a return stroke extending almost the whole width. The published crop has an angular left junction and a shorter curled return. Two fresh readers judged 17 separately coded running or display marks from four traditions, keeping each source orientation. They agreed on 89 of 90 jointly resolved feature judgments, with 29 judgments uncertain for one or both readers. The conjunction of an upright, sweep, aperture and turn occurs jointly in seven selected marks: two Ottoman signatures, a Greek separator, a Greek running form, a Latin notarial sign and two enlarged Voynich marks. Both Ottoman signatures place the long nested loops left of the center, with no required left-third descending shaft, linked right loop or under-return. No main-panel mark receives two affirmative readings on all ordered conditions, with four unresolved. The supplementary f76v scout, rated separately, satisfies the ordered conditions for both readers despite visible differences from the published p84 stroke outline. Thus the coarse geometry recurs outside the proposed pairing, and the ordered check still allows visibly different ink outlines within the manuscript. These role-mixed controls bound the specificity of visual features. Exact source provenance and proposed phonetic assignments remain open.
check: Establish the p84 crop on a primary unannotated page, with a document identifier, locus and overlay coordinates. Freeze which strokes constitute the proposed P, attached upright and reverse path, including orientation and allowed gaps. Sample complete equivalently placed components across independent manuscripts in each role, matched on aspect and visible shaft and aperture counts. Repeat with readers who see neutral filenames and only the specimen pixels. Score exact components and contact order separately from the four coarse shape features, retain uncertain junctions, and report comparisons by document.

declared_protocol.role: Compare visible ink geometry of medieval running and display marks. The p84 image defines predicted geometry. It is an annotated published crop and its position and role need independent verification. The article's p92 comparison is a separate Ottoman display specimen.

source_component_reading.p84: The paper rotates a Latin P 90 degrees clockwise in the yellow-highlighted area. It places a blue annotation at the end of the down-curved return and interprets the horizontal continuation leftward as YER/YAR. The uncolored upright in the photograph and the proposed joined I appear in the p84–85 account.
source_component_reading.orientation: Keep the source orientation of each entire specimen. The cited 90-degree rotation defines the proposed P component. It does not license rotation or reflection of a scored image.
source_component_reading.tolerance: Estimate fractions in the bounded visible dark-ink motif. A path must turn or touch within approximately one local ink-stroke width. If overlap, fading, or the crop hides that decision, mark uncertain. No adding bridges, following guides in the article, or treating a printed watermark as ink.

fields.U: Any near-vertical dark-ink shaft spanning at least 30 percent of motif height.
fields.S: Any plainly connected near-horizontal sweep spanning at least half the motif width, with slope within about 20 degrees.
fields.L: Any clearly bounded interior aperture traced by ink. A curl with an open gap is not enough.
fields.R: Any curved stroke whose direction clearly reverses and continues back alongside part of itself.
fields.A: A shaft descends from a junction with the qualifying sweep in the leftmost third of the motif and extends down at least 30 percent of motif height.
fields.B: A truly enclosed loop is visibly joined to that same sweep in the rightmost third of the motif.
fields.C: The right-end path from that same linked loop returns left under the sweep for at least one fifth of the motif width.

rules.read: Record yes, no, or uncertain for each field. Keep nearby text and other stray marks out of the motif. Make no linguistic or provenance classification.
rules.coarse_geometry: U, S, L and R must all be yes.
rules.ordered_geometry: S, A, B and C must all be yes.
rules.consensus: A yes or no is jointly resolved only when both readers agree on that value. A strict joint positive requires every field to be yes for both readers.
rules.comparators: Keep marks in running text separate from the imperial signatures, Greek separators, Latin initials, notarial display signs, and large Voynich flourish. Select within each role by visible connected units and aspect range where feasible. Record width-to-height, visibly resolved shaft and loop counts, roles and source documents. Contrasts across distinct display purposes or with obviously different geometric complexity are descriptive.
rules.limit: Two readers may share model-family priors. Recognizable script form may remain. No prevalence or significance claim from these deliberately selected archival controls.

source_description.p84–85: The author illustrates a claimed Latin P turned 90 degrees clockwise and attached to a preceding I-like upright. A blue mark indicates the proposed end of a downward curve. The leftward extension is assigned YER/YAR. The terminal reading retains alternatives.
source_description.p92: Five overlapping colored traces mark proposed contents of a short Mehmed II signature. They include X marks, loops and Roman-letter outlines, Runic N and a UÇ/UC tamga, verticals, and an 8-like S/Ş figure. Writing is proposed bottom-to-top. One colored connection may be a pen transition without a sound assignment.
source_description.source_uncertainty: The original figure, official companion tables and the p89 lookalike do not yield the exact unmarked locus. The p89 example has a different second crossbar and left hook. The reading identified by the p90 link is a different many-loop glyph.

localization_scout.scope: 204 files with numbered folio labels from 213 manifest canvases, including foldouts. Excluded nine covers, binding and calibration images. About 13.77 MB of thumbnails with a maximum edge of 600 or 800 pixels, and four native confirmation crops. Kept at most four public image downloads concurrent.
localization_scout.method: Used localized red-channel ink contrast with the blue overlay and cut-paper edges masked, and independently a centerline trace. Considered 22 widths from 15 to 326 pixels, five feature angles spanning -14 to 14 degrees and three trace angles from -10 to 10, in the original orientation. A local normalized correlation ranked candidates. These allowed small angular changes only for locating scans. The masked interpretation test keeps images unrotated.

strongest_examined_enlarged_shape_match.rejection: Closed triangle at the left cap and a return nearly as long as the upper sweep. The paper crop has a sharper open corner and a short upward-curled reverse segment.

reader_blinding.primary: Two fresh readers received the same 17 tiles in neutral folders, without their source, candidate statement or comparison role. One saw the shuffled sheets forward and the other in the reverse order, including reversed within-sheet orders.
reader_blinding.disclosure: Both readers recognized some silhouettes as tughra-like and some ornaments as notarial or rosette-like. Neither recognized an exact source or confidently read a background label. Pale archive print was visible for some motifs. The two readers may share model-family priors.

"""Prepare coded archival crops without rotating or redrawing strokes."""

from hashlib import sha256
import json
from pathlib import Path
import random

import numpy as np
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageOps
from scipy import ndimage


HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
RAW = HERE / "raw"
DESTINATION = HERE / "blind"

# In source pixels, after the initial source download or PDF rasterization.
DISPLAY = [
    ("voynich", "enlarged text feature", "voynich-f1r-crop.jpg", (125, 30, 620, 281)),
    ("voynich", "enlarged text feature", "voynich-f8r.jpg", (137, 450, 302, 556)),
    ("ottoman", "imperial signature", "ottoman-1468-head.jpg", (7, 4, 488, 279)),
    ("ottoman", "imperial signature", "ottoman-1477-head.jpg", (5, 4, 532, 206)),
    ("greek", "separator", "greek-1476-239r.jpg", (423, 452, 532, 520)),
    ("greek", "separator", "greek-1476-239r.jpg", (660, 457, 758, 529)),
    ("latin", "charter initial", "marseille-1425.jpg", (66, 34, 200, 255)),
    ("latin", "notarial mark", "marseille-1425.jpg", (866, 1361, 1000, 1455)),
    ("latin", "notarial mark", "sweden-1477-sign.jpg", (26, 40, 568, 1090)),
]

# Rectangles containing ordinary body writing, away from the selected display components.
RUNNING = [
    ("voynich", "voynich-f1r-crop.jpg", (465, 226, 824, 397), 1),
    ("voynich", "voynich-f8r.jpg", (540, 1110, 940, 1300), 1),
    ("ottoman", "ottoman-1468-page.jpg", (383, 643, 662, 1163), 1),
    ("ottoman", "ottoman-1477-page.jpg", (358, 572, 714, 1145), 1),
    ("greek", "greek-1476-239r.jpg", (199, 260, 832, 427), 2),
    ("latin", "marseille-1425.jpg", (145, 155, 777, 447), 2),
]


def bounding_candidates(image, region):
    gray = np.asarray(image.crop(region).convert("L"), dtype=np.float32)
    baseline = ndimage.gaussian_filter(gray, sigma=7)
    strong_ink = baseline - gray >= 21
    labels, count = ndimage.label(strong_ink, structure=np.ones((3, 3), np.uint8))
    areas = np.bincount(labels.ravel())
    found = []
    for component, bounds in enumerate(ndimage.find_objects(labels, count), start=1):
        vertical, horizontal = bounds
        top, bottom, left, right = vertical.start, vertical.stop, horizontal.start, horizontal.stop
        width, height = right - left, bottom - top
        if not (15 <= width <= 170 and 15 <= height <= 105 and 0.75 <= width / height <= 4.0):
            continue
        if areas[component] < max(35, 0.038 * width * height):
            continue
        if min(left, top, gray.shape[1] - right, gray.shape[0] - bottom) < 4:
            continue
        found.append((top, left, right, bottom))
    # Choose the first qualifying separate components in a fixed top-to-bottom band ordering.
    found.sort(key=lambda box: (box[0] // 35, box[1], box[0], box[3]))
    for top, left, right, bottom in found:
        yield region[0] + left - 4, region[1] + top - 4, region[0] + right + 4, region[1] + bottom + 4


def tile(image, crop):
    gray = ImageOps.autocontrast(image.crop(crop).convert("L"), cutoff=(0.5, 2))
    resized = ImageOps.contain(gray, (240, 144), method=Image.Resampling.LANCZOS)
    tile = Image.new("L", (260, 165), 255)
    tile.paste(resized, ((tile.width - resized.width) // 2, (tile.height - resized.height) // 2))
    return tile


def write_sheet(rows, filename):
    columns = 3
    height = ((len(rows) + columns - 1) // columns) * 190
    sheet = Image.new("L", (columns * 269, height), 255)
    drawer = ImageDraw.Draw(sheet)
    for index, row in enumerate(rows):
        x = index % columns * 269
        y = index // columns * 190
        code = row["code"]
        sheet.paste(Image.open(DESTINATION / f"{code}.png"), (x + 4, y + 21))
        drawer.text((x + 9, y + 5), code, fill=10)
    sheet.save(DESTINATION / filename)


def main():
    records = []
    for tradition, role, filename, box in DISPLAY:
        records.append({"tradition": tradition, "role": role, "input": filename, "crop_xyxy": box})
    for tradition, filename, region, quota in RUNNING:
        image = Image.open(RAW / filename)
        candidates = list(bounding_candidates(image, region))
        if len(candidates) < quota:
            raise ValueError(f"Only {len(candidates)} eligible running components in {filename}")
        for box in candidates[:quota]:
            records.append({
                "tradition": tradition, "role": "running ink component", "input": filename,
                "crop_xyxy": box, "source_roi_xyxy": region,
                "eligible_components_in_region": len(candidates),
            })
    random.Random(36284).shuffle(records)
    DESTINATION.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    for index, row in enumerate(records, 31):
        code = f"M{index}"
        row["code"] = code
        left, upper, right, lower = row["crop_xyxy"]
        row["crop_aspect_ratio"] = round((right - left) / (lower - upper), 4)
        input_path = RAW / row["input"]
        row["source_sha256"] = sha256(input_path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
        output = DESTINATION / f"{code}.png"
        with Image.open(input_path) as image:
            tile(image, row["crop_xyxy"]).save(output)
        row["tile_sha256"] = sha256(output.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
    (HERE / "protocol" / "key.json").write_text(json.dumps(records, indent=2) + "\n")
    for number in range((len(records) + 5) // 6):
        rows = records[number * 6:(number + 1) * 6]
        write_sheet(rows, f"sheet{number + 1}.png")
        write_sheet(list(reversed(rows)), f"reverse{number + 1}.png")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

from pathlib import Path
import argparse
import json

import numpy as np
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
from scipy.fft import rfft2, irfft2, next_fast_len
from scipy.ndimage import gaussian_filter, distance_transform_edt, maximum_filter


HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
INPUT = HERE.parent / "raw/p84-000.jpg"
REGION = (22, 63, 438, 274)
WIDTHS = (15, 18, 21, 25, 29, 34, 39, 45, 52, 60, 69, 79, 91, 105,
          121, 140, 161, 186, 214, 248, 285, 326)
REFERENCE_PATHS = (
    ((47, 184), (44, 180), (46, 174), (52, 166), (63, 162), (76, 156), (90, 154), (103, 150)),
    ((103, 126), (101, 148), (99, 177), (96, 202), (93, 231), (93, 252), (97, 262), (105, 266)),
    ((103, 127), (127, 129), (170, 132), (216, 132), (259, 126), (294, 124), (333, 124),
     (374, 121), (401, 113)),
    ((403, 116), (402, 103), (400, 94), (400, 86), (405, 79), (413, 80), (419, 85), (421, 94),
     (415, 107), (406, 115), (403, 133), (392, 144), (380, 152), (357, 163), (341, 167),
     (315, 174), (298, 172), (289, 164), (289, 151)),
)
BLUE = ((244, 180), (265, 162), (286, 149), (303, 142))


def path_image(paths, width):
    mask = Image.new("L", (REGION[2] - REGION[0], REGION[3] - REGION[1]))
    draw = ImageDraw.Draw(mask)
    for path in paths:
        xy = [(x-REGION[0], y-REGION[1]) for x,y in path]
        draw.line(xy, fill=255, width=width, joint="curve")
    return np.asarray(mask, dtype=np.float32) / 255


def standard_ink(a, sigma, local):
    high = gaussian_filter(a, sigma) - a
    kept = high / np.sqrt(gaussian_filter(high * high, local) + 5)
    return np.clip(kept, -3.5, 3.5)


def target_parts(mode):
    rgb = np.asarray(Image.open(INPUT).convert("RGB").crop(REGION), dtype=np.float32)
    red = rgb[:,:,0]
    paper = (rgb[:,:,0] - rgb[:,:,2] > 13) & (rgb[:,:,1] < 236)
    safe = (distance_transform_edt(paper) >= 6) & (path_image((BLUE,), 13) == 0)
    t = standard_ink(gaussian_filter(red, 1.0), 5, 8)
    paths = tuple(path_image((path,), 8) for path in REFERENCE_PATHS)
    full = np.maximum.reduce(paths)
    support = gaussian_filter(path_image(REFERENCE_PATHS, 29), 2) * safe
    if mode == "traced":
        t = gaussian_filter(full, 2.2)
    elif mode == "feature":
        t = np.maximum(t, 0) * gaussian_filter(full, 3)
    return t.astype(np.float32), support.astype(np.float32)


def array_transform(a, width, angle, mirror, size=None):
    im = Image.fromarray(a)
    if mirror:
        im = im.transpose(Image.Transpose.FLIP_LEFT_RIGHT)
    if angle:
        im = im.rotate(angle, resample=Image.Resampling.BICUBIC, expand=True, fillcolor=0)
    if size is None:
        size = width, max(1, round(im.height * width / im.width))
    return np.asarray(im.resize(size, Image.Resampling.BILINEAR), dtype=np.float32)


def make_templates(mode, angles, mirrors):
    t, m = target_parts(mode)
    for mirror in mirrors:
        for angle in angles:
            for width in WIDTHS:
                target = array_transform(t, width, angle, mirror)
                hit = target.shape[::-1]
                mask = np.clip(array_transform(m, width, angle, mirror, hit), 0, 1)
                if mask.sum() <= 0:
                    continue
                target = mask * (target - (target * mask).sum() / mask.sum())
                total = np.maximum(target, 0).sum()
                if total > 0:
                    yield (mode, angle, mirror, width, target / total, mask)


def score_at(plane, templ, support, y, x):
    h,w = templ.shape
    arr = plane[y:y+h,x:x+w]
    centered = arr - (support * arr).sum() / support.sum()
    target_energy = ((templ * templ)/np.maximum(support, 1e-6)).sum()
    ink_energy = (support * centered * centered).sum()
    return float((centered * templ).sum() / np.sqrt(max(target_energy * ink_energy, 1e-6)))


def page_search(img, templates, best_n):
    plane = standard_ink(np.asarray(img.getchannel("R"), dtype=np.float32), 2.1, 3.8)
    H,W = plane.shape
    shape = (next_fast_len(H + max(k[4].shape[0] for k in templates) - 1),
             next_fast_len(W + max(k[4].shape[1] for k in templates) - 1))
    spectrum = rfft2(plane, shape)
    found = []
    for mode, angle, mirror, width, t, mask in templates:
        h,w = t.shape
        if (h >= H) or (w >= W):
            continue
        total = irfft2(spectrum * rfft2(t[::-1,::-1], shape), shape)
        vals = total[h-1:H,w-1:W].copy()
        hits = []
        for _ in range(best_n):
            vy,vx = np.unravel_index(vals.argmax(), vals.shape)
            score = vals[vy,vx]
            if not np.isfinite(score):
                break
            ncc = score_at(plane,t,mask,vy,vx)
            hits.append(dict(corr=float(ncc),response=float(score),x=int(vx),y=int(vy),
                             w=w,h=h,angle=angle,mirror=mirror,mode=mode,thumb=[W,H]))
            gap = max(7,width//4)
            vals[max(0,vy-gap):vy+gap,max(0,vx-gap):vx+gap] = -np.inf
        found.extend(sorted(hits, key=lambda z: z["corr"], reverse=True)[:3])
    return sorted(found, key=lambda z: z["corr"], reverse=True)


def main():
    p=argparse.ArgumentParser()
    p.add_argument("--angles", type=int, nargs="+",default=[0])
    p.add_argument("--mode", choices=["learned","feature","traced"],default="feature")
    p.add_argument("--output", default="search-results.json")
    p.add_argument("--mirror", action="store_true")
    p.add_argument("--id", nargs="+")
    p.add_argument("--peaks", type=int, default=8)
    args=p.parse_args()
    labels = {x["id"]: x for x in json.loads((HERE/"yale_pages.json").read_text())}
    images = sorted((HERE/"yale").glob("*.jpg"))
    if args.id is not None:
        images = [p for p in images if p.stem in args.id]
    templates = list(make_templates(args.mode,args.angles,[True] if args.mirror else [False]))
    output=[]
    for f in images:
        im=Image.open(f).convert("RGB")
        scores=page_search(im,templates,args.peaks)
        output.extend(dict(found,id=f.stem,label=labels[f.stem]["label"]) for found in scores)
        print(f.stem,labels[f.stem]["label"],scores[0],flush=True)
    (HERE/args.output).write_text(json.dumps(sorted(output,key=lambda z:z["corr"],reverse=True),indent=2)+"\n")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
